title: DoseFolio
description: Review medication names and source directions, search your imported list, and export a personal review with DoseFolio. No dose tracking or interaction advice.
workflow: Search medications, mark entries reviewed in the current session, inspect source directions and allergies, and export the review.
subject: Medication list review & export
label: Notes from the review desk
headline: How we built a medication review desk
summary: Why DoseFolio separates finding a medication, reading its directions, and marking an entry reviewed.
sections: DoseFolio is organized around find, check and take away. Search narrows an imported medication list. A review mark records which entries the visitor has read in the current session. Export produces a copy for a later conversation. Keeping these actions separate prevents a checkbox from looking like a medication administration record. Checking an entry never means a dose was taken.

The frontend is a React application served as static files. Its connection requests go to a separate Node service, which uses FinchNode Hosted Connect and the production API. That server keeps the API key outside the browser and ties a temporary session to this site’s origin. DoseFolio receives the categories authorized for that session rather than a browser credential that could query arbitrary patients.

The review desk displays supplied medication details rather than generating a dosing schedule. A recorded direction may be incomplete, old or different from a current instruction. The app does not resolve that difference, check interactions or recommend changes. The useful outcome is a list of entries to clarify with a clinician or pharmacist, with the source wording available to support the discussion.

Review marks belong to the current interface session. They are not sent back to a medical record and should not be treated as an adherence history. An exported review is a separate file under the visitor’s control. Ending the connection removes access here, but does not erase a file already downloaded. This distinction is part of the workflow, not an extra promise about clinical accuracy.

The code implements the production connection path, while live activation is still pending. An unavailable connection produces a setup message instead of a sample medication list. DoseFolio has its own review-focused interface and public repository, with a clear boundary between the connection adapter and the review desk. The implementation can be inspected in source; deployment alone is not evidence of real patient connectivity.
guideIntro: Explore medication-list review, the meaning of source status, and the difference between a temporary review checklist and an authorized clinical record.
finchnodeContext: DoseFolio receives medication and allergy information through FinchNode, then adds its own temporary review checklist. A checked box records progress in this interface; it does not certify a medication list or update a prescription.

articles.title: How to review a medication list in DoseFolio
articles.description: Search recorded medications, compare source directions and export your review progress without changing prescriptions or source status.

sections.heading: Read the three counters correctly
paragraphs: DoseFolio distinguishes the number of recorded medications, entries marked active by the source, and entries reviewed during the current session. Those counts answer different questions. A source status is part of the imported record; the reviewed count reflects clicks in this workspace.

sections.heading: Find and inspect an entry
paragraphs: Use “Find a medication” to filter by the displayed medication label. Clear the search when you want to see the full list again. Read the directions and frequency supplied with an entry. A missing instruction is shown as missing, rather than replaced with a guessed dose.
items: Compare the label with the entry you meant to inspect.
Read the recorded directions and the displayed source context.
Mark the entry reviewed only after reading it.
Keep unresolved questions for a pharmacist or clinician.

sections.heading: Know what the export includes
paragraphs: The text export includes the full imported medication list, each entry’s review flag, and its supplied dosage text or a missing-directions label. A search filter does not restrict the exported list. The file is a personal review aid; it is not a new prescription or a clinically reconciled medication list.

sections.heading: Use the checklist within its limits
paragraphs: DoseFolio displays allergies from the same authorized response for reference. It does not calculate drug interactions or advise changes to treatment. Review flags are temporary and do not write back to the source. The connected workflow remains subject to production activation.

questions.question: Does searching change which medications are exported?
questions.answer: No. DoseFolio’s review export uses the complete returned medication list, with review flags, even when the screen is filtered.

questions.question: Does “reviewed” mean safe to take?
questions.answer: No. It means you checked that entry in this session. The app does not assess medication safety.

articles.title: Medication review flags are different from source status
articles.description: Understand why DoseFolio keeps “reviewed this session” separate from an imported medication’s active status and recorded directions.

sections.heading: A status field belongs to its source
paragraphs: The active count reads the status supplied with each medication. DoseFolio does not infer current use from the age of an entry, its appearance in the list, or the presence of directions. If the record raises a question about current treatment, the interface gives you an entry to discuss rather than an answer to assume.

sections.heading: A review flag belongs to this visit to the app
paragraphs: Checking an entry stores its ID in the interface’s review state. It does not alter the medication object. This separation lets the same recorded information support different personal review sessions without silently turning a checklist action into a clinical edit.

sections.heading: The export preserves the distinction
paragraphs: Each exported line says whether the entry was reviewed in this session. The review label accompanies the medication text; it does not replace the source’s status. Someone reading the file should treat it as a record of your review activity, with any unanswered questions handled separately.

sections.heading: What an operator can extend
paragraphs: A business extending DoseFolio could add a note field or improve how discrepancies are displayed. Such additions should state whether they are local annotations or updates to another system. The implemented service is read-only, and patient imports are awaiting activation.

questions.question: Can the checklist change a medication from active to inactive?
questions.answer: No. The interface keeps review progress separate from the imported status field.

finchnode.heading: FinchNode carries the record; DoseFolio tracks the review
finchnode.text: The medication and allergy categories in this implementation arrive through FinchNode. DoseFolio’s contribution is the review experience layered on that response. Keeping the two kinds of state distinct makes it possible to explain exactly what a checked box means.
